g.text: Continuous Estimated Tardiness Reward & Anti-Tardiness Learning
How PPO perceives state urgency, calculates dense step penalties, and learns optimal dispatching rules
State Observation: What the Agent Sees Before Action
• Workload balance & idle tool ratio per workstation group
Time-Accurate Schedule: Baseline Estimate vs. Actual Dispatch
A. Initial Ideal Estimate at t = 0 (reset): Zero Queueing, Zero Setup Loss
• Code calculation at reset: initial_ect = 5 + 8 + 5 = 18 min ≤ Due (22) ⇒ curr_est_tardiness[j] = 0.0
B. Actual Dispatch of Job j at Step k: Machine Queueing & Setup Delay
• Step k evaluation: new_ect = best_finish (18) + rem_proc (5) = 23 min ⇒ Overrun past Due Date by 1.0 min!
The Reinforcement Learning Loop: How PPO Eliminates Tardiness
L^CLIP(θ) = Ê [ min(r̂_t Â_t, clip · Â_t) ]
Prioritizes jobs where Slack → 0 before safe jobs.
Always saves Super_Hot (10×) over Regular (1×) jobs.
Avoids redundant setup time to prevent tool blockage.
Action Masking blocks finished jobs automatically.
r_t = - (1 / scale) · [ w_M · ΔC_max + w_S · S_best + w_T · (ΔEstTard_j / N_jobs) + w_I · (I_best / 10) ]
• ΔEstTard_j = max(0, new_est_tard - curr_est_tardiness[j]): Penalizes any scheduling decision that delays job completion past its due date.
• Credit Assignment Resolved: The gradient directly attributes the penalty to the specific dispatch action that caused the delay, enabling fast convergence.
